question: Let $A=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For a permutation $P=(P(1),P(2),\ldots,P(n))$ of the elements of $A$, let $P(1)$ denote the first element of $P$. Find the number of all such permutations $P$ so that for all $i,j\in A$: if $i<j<P(1)$, then $j$ appears before $i$ in $P$; and if $P(1)<i<j$, then $i$ appears before $j$ in $P.
